projectName: Portfolio - Sanity CMS Foundation & Content Migration
description: Plan-first epic to make Sanity the working CMS for the portfolio: align connections, complete schema coverage, create deterministic migration scripts, and switch the Next.js app to Sanity-backed reads with a safe fallback path.

planSummary.goal: Make the Sanity studio and the Next.js app work together as one content system without manual content entry.
approach: Normalize the Sanity project and dataset connections across app, studio, and environment files.
Map every existing JSON dataset to a Sanity model or a deliberate normalized equivalent.
Create missing schemas for content groups that are present in the repo data but not yet modeled.
Write idempotent migration scripts that seed, refresh, and report on content import progress.
Switch the app to Sanity-first reads only after parity is proven and fallback behavior is verified.
Keep JSON files in place during migration so the app can still run while the CMS is being populated.
nonGoals: Redesigning the public UI beyond what is required to consume CMS data.
Replacing the existing portfolio architecture with a different framework.
Manually entering content as the primary migration method.
Deleting the JSON source of truth before parity and cutover are complete.

reason: Make Sanity the working CMS for the portfolio content in portfolio-resources/data
Establish reliable studio, preview, slug, and reference wiring before migrating content
Automate content population with repeatable scripts instead of manual entry
Keep the existing Next.js app stable while the data source is switched over
Preserve branch history while restarting development from the latest main tip

contentInventory.notes: Currently has no matching Sanity schema; must be modeled explicitly or folded into a singleton profile document.
Already represented by studio/schemaTypes/experience.ts, but field normalization is needed because the schema uses role/company and the JSON uses position/company.
Already represented by studio/schemaTypes/project.ts, but slug, ordering, and link precedence must be preserved during migration.
Current schema covers certification, certificationCategory, and certificationIssuer, but the JSON has a flatter shape that must be normalized into references.
Current schema covers galleryImage and galleryCategory, but the import must preserve file names with spaces and encode media paths safely.
Current techStack schema groups technologies by category; the migration must transform the flat JSON into category buckets.
Current post, author, and category schemas exist; slug uniqueness and publication flags must be normalized for editorial use.

migrationOrder: 1. Canonical project/dataset alignment and preview wiring
2. Singleton homepage content: heroSection, aboutSection, siteSettings, resume, techStack
3. Taxonomy/reference sets: category, certificationCategory, certificationIssuer, galleryCategory, author
4. Core collections: experience, project, certification, galleryImage, post
5. Missing collections: profile, social links, memberships, recommendations if retained in CMS
6. Sanity-first app read layer and fallback removal after parity
7. Draft preview, revalidation, and editorial handoff
phase1ImplementationChecklist: Confirm the canonical Sanity project ID and dataset used by both the root app and the studio.
Record the authoritative environment variables for read, write, preview, and revalidation access.
Compare every JSON file in portfolio-resources/data against the current Sanity schemas.
Mark each collection as one of: existing schema, existing schema with field normalization, new schema required, or singleton normalization required.
Define the slug rules for posts, authors, category references, issuer references, and any future URL-backed entities.
Define the reference rules for certification issuers, certification categories, gallery categories, blog authors, and blog categories.
Define ordering rules for experiences, projects, certifications, gallery items, and homepage singleton sections.
Decide where social links, memberships, recommendations, and profile data will live in Sanity.
Write the migration contract for every file: source file, target model, required transforms, and validation checks.
Identify any media asset filename normalization needed before import.
Freeze the Phase 1 mapping before any migration or app cutover code is written.

The canonical project/dataset values are fixed.

stories.title: Audit Content Inventory and Model Coverage
acceptanceCriteria: Map every JSON dataset in portfolio-resources/data to the correct Sanity document or singleton type
Identify which schema files already cover the source data and which ones need to be added or normalized
Define slug, reference, ordering, and preview rules for each collection
Document field-level mismatches between JSON keys and schema field names
Confirm which content groups are singleton-managed and which are collection-managed

stories.title: Stabilize Studio Connectivity and Preview Configuration
acceptanceCriteria: Sanity projectId and dataset are confirmed and documented for the repo
The studio config exposes the portfolio content types in a clear structure
Preview and presentation settings point to the correct local and production preview targets
Draft mode or equivalent preview wiring is available for the Next.js app
The studio can be built locally without breaking existing config
The root app and studio read the same canonical project connection values

stories.title: Complete Schema Coverage and Normalize Slugs
acceptanceCriteria: Add or normalize schemas for any content collections not yet represented in studio/schemaTypes
Ensure hero, about, experience, project, certification, gallery, blog, resume, tech stack, and site settings have a consistent mapping
Add missing profile, social link, and membership schemas if those collections are migrated into Sanity
Define slug generation rules for blog posts and any content that needs stable human-readable URLs
Keep preview definitions useful for editorial navigation in the studio
Normalize field names where the JSON source and the schema currently differ

stories.title: Build Idempotent Migration and Seed Scripts
acceptanceCriteria: Create repeatable scripts that can seed or refresh Sanity from the JSON source of truth
Support dry-run mode so the import can be verified before writing data
Upload or map media assets and preserve image references correctly
Resolve document references, singleton updates, and slug fields without duplicate writes
Generate a migration report showing created, updated, skipped, and failed records
Allow reruns after a partial import without creating duplicate documents

stories.title: Switch the App Data Layer to Sanity-First Reads
acceptanceCriteria: The Next.js app reads Sanity content first for all migrated content groups
The existing JSON data layer remains as a controlled fallback until cutover is complete
Blog slugs and content lookups resolve correctly from CMS data

Type safety remains intact across the migration boundary
Content queries fail gracefully when a record has not yet been migrated

technicalNotes.risk: A partial data switch can produce inconsistent rendering if one section is migrated before its dependencies

stories.title: Implement Draft Preview and Editorial Workflow
acceptanceCriteria: Editors can preview changed homepage and blog content from the studio

stories.title: Run Cutover Validation and Publish the CMS Runbook
